correctness.rationale: The zero-sum powered-distance quadratic form splits into strictly negative leaf residuals, a symmetric scalar \(f_q(p)\), and an antisymmetric determinant \(qg_q(p)\). Its unique critical root in \(1<p\le2\) follows from strict monotonicity of \(\phi(p)=(3/2)^p-1-2^{-p}\). For \(q\ge2\), the antisymmetric determinant stays positive until the symmetric root by concavity at \(p_0\) and monotonicity of \(g_q\). Thus the first loss of negative type has exactly the claimed one-dimensional equality space, with minimal Hilbert dimension from Schoenberg centering. The four-vertex path is handled separately. The inverse-leaf-count asymptotics follow by Taylor inversion. Independent BFS and rational finite checks corroborate, but do not prove, the universal classification.

value.rationale: The exactly evaluated one-hub star is a natural benchmark for finite-tree generalized roundness. A tree with two branching hubs is the minimal nonstar branching interaction; the classification gives an exact all-size exponent, exact unique first-loss nullspace, sharp critical Euclidean rank, and explicit O(1/q) convergence to the tree extremal bound 1. The strict comparison with induced stars proves a genuine new interaction between branches, not a routine reparameterization or a single numerical example.
